claim: Let \(m_{\mathrm{FPP}}(S^1)\) be the least cardinality of a finite \(T_0\)-space with the fixed point property and weak homotopy type \(S^1\). Then \(10 \le m_{\mathrm{FPP}}(S^1) \le 14\).

correctness.rationale: For cardinality at most 9, the small-set FPP theorem gives connected collapsibility. Baclawski Proposition 6.5 and Corollary 6.9 imply pseudo-cone order complex, whose realization is contractible, so first homology vanishes. McCord transfers this homology obstruction to the finite T0-space, excluding weak circle type. Barmak Lemma 10 supplies a 14-point FPP space of weak type S1. The two inequalities therefore follow without computational assumptions.

evidence: Rutkowski 1989 treats small finite FPP posets.
Baclawski 2012 proves the collapse/pseudo-cone mechanism and contractibility of pseudo cones.
Barmak 2013 proves existence of finite FPP representatives in every connected compact CW weak homotopy type and gives a 14-point circle example.
broader_coverage.reasoning: The broader theorems cover the ingredients but neither side alone implies the numerical bracket. The lower obstruction and upper witness have to be combined.

The claim is a synthesis of a small-poset lower obstruction and a later explicit upper witness; it is not presented as a priority claim. Direct inspection of the most relevant accessible primary texts found the ingredients but not the combined bound.
residual_risks: The direct Rutkowski 1989 full text was inaccessible, so its exact wording was checked through a later explicit restatement rather than page-level inspection of the original.
Targeted search cannot prove that no later paper or book has already stated the same 10-to-14 synthesis.
The claim does not determine which of the five remaining cardinalities is exact.

value.rationale: Minimum size is a natural invariant for finite fixed-point representatives of a weak homotopy type. For S1, the claim reduces the unresolved problem to five consecutive sizes, 10 through 14. This is a meaningful finite cutoff tied to an explicit classical construction and a sharp small-cardinality obstruction, not an arbitrary numerical slice.
